verdict.rationale: Neon documents real performance-insight capabilities — the MCP server's 'List Slow Queries', 'Explain SQL Statement', and 'inspect_database' tool (which runs the same 15 read-only checks as `neon inspect db`: table/index sizes, unused indexes, stalled queries with waits/blockers, cache hit rate, bloat, replication state) — giving a platform engineer slow-query and index-recommendation data via CLI/MCP. However, the evidence never describes a dedicated built-in console 'insights' dashboard view; the data is exposed through CLI commands and MCP tool calls rather than a persistent UI panel. Missing for 10: a documented native console insights/dashboard UI, explicit index-recommendation feature (vs. unused-index detection), and independent/hands-on confirmation of this workflow.
